review_comments.body:
** Minor** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Quick win** **Reject a constraint that already belongs to another problem.** The duplicate guard at lines 2040-2043 matches only when `_problem` is this problem. A constraint added to a second problem keeps the second owner. A later `p.addConstraint(c)` then passes the guard. It appends `c` to `p.constrs` again and overwrites `c.index`. The first entry no longer matches its index. This path requires one `Constraint` object shared across two problems. The API does not document that pattern, and the PR's duplicate check covers only the same problem. Treat this as a narrow misuse case. Consider rejecting a constraint whose `_problem` is a different problem, before any state changes. This changes an operation that succeeds today, so confirm that no caller depends on it. A membership scan of `self.constrs` would also catch this case, but it adds O(n) cost to each add.

Adding the same constraint object twice to one problem now raises ValueError before any state changes. A narrow edge case remains: reusing one constraint object across two problems can still produce a duplicate entry. This is unlikely in normal use and can be handled as a follow-up.

The change rejects duplicate constraints before altering the model, strengthening state consistency. No introduced or worsened risk materially affecting security, failure containment, rollback, or ownership guarantees was established. **Retained concerns** No architecture-level concerns identified.
Security review details

**Security Blast Radius** - _inferred_ — The changed behavior is confined to caller-supplied objects entering the existing in-process registration method. The inspected change adds rejection checks, not a new remote entrypoint, privileged operation, or downstream authority. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — The guard is a model-consistency control, not an authorization boundary. It requires the constraint's owning-problem pointer to identify the receiver, an in-range index, and identity with the object stored at that index. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _inferred_ — The guard does not establish global ownership or atomic registration: cross-problem reuse can overwrite the single owning-problem pointer, and successful registration remains a sequence of mutations without added synchronization. These limitations predate this PR and are not retained as introduced or worsened concerns.

Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title names the actual change: Problem.addConstraint now rejects adding the same Constraint twice. It is concise, specific, and follows a conventional commit style. It matches the raw summary and the linked issue `#2326` objective.
Full details: Description check

**Explanation** The description states the root cause (addConstraint did not check for an existing registration, so constr.index was overwritten and the constraint was appended twice). It explains the fix (ValueError raised before state mutation) and the test added. This matches the raw summary and the PR objectives.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** [`#2326`] requires that `Problem.addConstraint` raise `ValueError` when the same `Constraint` object is added twice, with `p.constrs` and `c.index` unchanged. The whole-PR diff adds a guard at the start of `addConstraint` in `python/cuopt/cuopt/linear_programming/problem.py`. The guard raises `ValueError` when the object is already at its recorded index in `self.constrs` and its `_problem` is this problem. It runs before `_reset_solved_values()`, `_invalidate_problem_cache()`, and the append/index assignment, so no state changes on rejection. The non-`Constraint` path also raises `ValueError`. The test `test_add_constraint_rejects_duplicate` in `test_python_API.py` covers the duplicate case and asserts that `constrs`, `index`, `ConstraintName`, and `NumConstraints` are unchanged. Limit: the guard depends on `index` and `_problem` being stored in `constr.__dict__`, which I did not confirm in the `Constraint` class. The test result is taken from the author's report; I did not run it.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check

**Explanation** The whole-PR diff touches only `problem.py` (the guard in `addConstraint`) and `test_python_API.py` (one new test). Both changes address the duplicate-constraint behavior described in `#2326`. No unrelated changes appear in the diff. The PR summary's line counts match the diff.
